steps.title: Claiming Candidates
steps.body: Claiming is the flip side of Pointing. When all candidates for a digit in a row or column fall inside the same 3×3 box, that line "claims" the digit and removes it from the rest of the box.

steps.title: Set the Stage
steps.body: We'll clear the easy singles so the claiming pattern pops. Keep notes on — claiming uses the pencil marks you already know.

steps.title: Highlight the 1s
steps.body: Tap any filled 1 to highlight where 1s already sit. Seeing the existing 1s makes it easier to spot where they can't go.

steps.title: Only in This Box
steps.body: Look at the top row. The only places for a 1 are the two highlighted cells inside the middle box. That means this row forces the 1 to stay inside this box.

steps.title: Apply the Claiming Move
steps.body: Select both candidate cells in the top row (columns 4 and 6). Because those are the only 1s in the row, the rest of this box can't contain a 1. The strategy will remove 1 from the other cells in the box.

steps.title: What Changed
steps.body: Claiming removed the 1 from the other cells in this box. Whenever a line claims a digit, scrub it from the rest of that box.

steps.title: Finish the Puzzle
steps.body: Use Claiming along with the singles and open pairs you've already learned to finish up!
